name: Ruth

objectives.text: Name Naomi, Ruth, and Boaz as the main people in the book of Ruth and tell one thing each person did
Recall Ruth's promise to go with Naomi and to make Naomi's people and God her own
Describe how Boaz showed kindness to Ruth while she gathered grain in his field
Identify actions in Ruth's story that show loyal kindness and give examples of similar actions toward family and friends
Retell the story of Ruth in order from the famine and Naomi's return to Bethlehem through the birth of Obed
Explain how God's law about gleaning provided food for poor people and foreigners like Ruth
Identify Obed, the son of Ruth and Boaz, as the grandfather of King David
Compare Orpah's choice to return to Moab with Ruth's choice to stay with Naomi using details from the text
Explain what a kinsman redeemer was in Israel and how Boaz filled that role for Naomi and Ruth
Trace how Naomi moves from emptiness and bitterness at her return to fullness at the birth of Obed
Explain the meaning of the Hebrew word hesed and identify where Ruth, Boaz, and the LORD each show it in the book
Locate Moab and Bethlehem on a map and explain why Ruth's identity as a Moabite mattered in Israel
Connect the setting of Ruth to the period of the judges and contrast its faithful characters with the disorder of that time
Analyze the literary structure of Ruth by outlining its four scenes and showing how the opening and closing sections mirror each other
Explain the levirate marriage custom and how it relates to Boaz's redemption of Elimelech's land and name
Interpret the significance of a Moabite woman appearing in the genealogy of Jesus Christ
Analyze the legal proceedings at the city gate including the elders, the witnesses, and the sandal exchange
Explain Ruth's place among the Writings in the Hebrew canon and its traditional reading at the Feast of Weeks compared with its place in English Bibles
Analyze how Ruth's words and actions present her as a Gentile who takes refuge under the wings of Israel's God
Evaluate the ways Boaz as kinsman redeemer foreshadows Christ as the Redeemer of God's people and where the comparison has limits
Evaluate how the book of Ruth displays God's providence working through ordinary events and human choices while rarely describing God acting directly
Defend from Ruth and related Scripture the Reformed teaching that God's saving purpose includes people from the nations
Synthesize the book of Ruth as a bridge from the period of the judges to the Davidic monarchy using its setting and closing genealogy

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (characters, gleaning, David's ancestry, Orpah and Ruth, kinsman redeemer, structure, Moabite in Christ's line, judges timeline, levirate marriage, Boaz as type of Christ, providence, Gentile inclusion, bridge to monarchy). Reframed the friendship application as an observable task of identifying and giving examples of loyal kindness. Merged the Naomi summary into a full ordered retelling. Added Ruth's vow, Boaz's kindness, gleaning law, Naomi's empty to full arc, hesed, Moab geography, the city gate proceedings, canonical placement and Feast of Weeks, and Ruth's refuge under God's wings. Replaced whole-chapter style references with verse ranges, added confessional anchors for providence, Christ as Redeemer, and the catholic church, and noted limits of typology.
